biography: Matías Rossi, a name now whispered with a mix of excitement and trepidation throughout the Brazilian racing scene, didn't come from racing royalty. He grew up in the favelas of São Paulo, karting on makeshift tracks carved into the dirt. His raw talent was undeniable, a relentless fire in his eyes even then. A chance encounter with a local businessman, impressed by Matías's daring overtakes during a street race, led to his first real kart. From there, he blazed through the junior ranks, his aggressive style earning him both victories and penalties. After a difficult start with AMM Vogel, where the team's machinery struggled to match his ambition, he returned to Full Time Sports, a team that understood his need for a car as fearless as he is. Now, at 25, Rossi stands at the peak of his abilities, ready to challenge the established order.
drivingStyle: Rossi's driving style is a high-risk, high-reward gamble. He attacks corners with an almost reckless abandon, pushing the car to its absolute limit and often beyond. He's known for his late braking and daring overtakes, moves that frequently leave rivals shaking their heads in disbelief, or nursing damaged bodywork. While his tire management could be improved, his ability to handle pressure is exceptional. He thrives in chaotic situations, often finding himself at the front when others falter.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing feud originating from a controversial collision in their Formula Vee days. Rossi accused Silva of deliberately blocking him, and the animosity has simmered ever since.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky socks, gifted to him by his grandmother, for every race.
Listens to a specific Brazilian samba song on repeat for 30 minutes before getting into the car to calm his nerves.
Taps the top of his helmet three times before the start of each race, a habit he picked up from a legendary F1 driver he admired growing up.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser. I'm here to win, and I'll do whatever it takes, within the rules of course, to get there."
careerHighlight: Winning the Brazilian Stock Car Championship in 2022 after a season-long battle, securing the title with a daring last-lap overtake in the final race, silencing his doubters and cementing his place as a force to be reckoned with.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the 2021 Interlagos 500 with only three laps remaining due to a mechanical failure, costing him a potential victory and leaving him devastated.
